title: Validate check 'fix' key is non-empty string in validate_checks (#3630)
summary: Replace silent str()-coercion of the optional 'fix' key in validate_checks with explicit isinstance(fix, str) and truthiness validation. When fix is present but not a non-empty string (false, 0, '', or a YAML list), log a warning and drop it so the config error surfaces at load time rather than as a runtime green-gate mystery. Aligned all three copies: shared/egg_config/validators.py (primary), config/repo_config.py (ImportError fallback), orchestrator/routes/pipelines/__init__.py (ImportError fallback). Added unit tests covering valid string, empty string, false/0, list, and absent key cases.

problem_statement.description: validate_checks in shared/egg_config/validators.py handles the optional 'fix' key with `if c.get('fix'): entry['fix'] = str(c['fix'])`. This causes two operator-hostile behaviors: (1) silent drop on falsy values (fix: '', fix: false, fix: 0) with no warning, leaving the operator with a configured fix: in repositories.yaml and a green gate that never self-heals; (2) str() coercion of non-strings — a YAML list like fix: [make fmt, make lint-fix] is coerced to the literal string "['make fmt', 'make lint-fix']" and handed to the check runner as a shell command, failing as a subprocess with a message that does not point back at the config.
problem_statement.grounded_against_tree: 2026-07-29; live issue #3630 body fetched via gh issue view; all three copies of validate_checks confirmed to exist and carry the identical buggy pattern.

validate_checks_locations.primary: shared/egg_config/validators.py:164-208 — canonical implementation, no logger currently imported
validate_checks_locations.fallback_repo_config: config/repo_config.py:363-392 — ImportError fallback, has module-level logger (egg.repo_config)

current_architecture.current_fix_handling: All three copies use `if c.get('fix'): entry['fix'] = str(c['fix'])` — falsy values silently dropped, non-strings str()-coerced
current_architecture.logging_pattern: repo_config.py uses logging.getLogger('egg.repo_config') with logger.warning(...) for config rejections; validators.py has no logging currently

findings.finding: Three copies of validate_checks exist with identical buggy fix handling: the primary in shared/egg_config/validators.py and two ImportError fallbacks in config/repo_config.py and orchestrator/routes/pipelines/__init__.py. All three must be aligned.
The current test test_values_coerced_to_strings asserts fix: 3 is coerced to fix: '3' — this test will need updating since integer fix values should now be rejected, not coerced.
The existing test_empty_fix_dropped tests fix: '' and fix: None but does not verify a warning is logged — it will need to be extended to assert the warning.
The full_command key has the same str()-coercion pattern but the issue explicitly scopes the fix to the 'fix' key only ('Do not refactor the surrounding validators'). full_command is left unchanged.
name and command keys are also str()-coerced but the issue says not to refactor surrounding validators — only fix key handling changes.

recommended_approach.fix_validation_logic: Replace `if c.get('fix'): entry['fix'] = str(c['fix'])` with: `if 'fix' in c: fix_val = c['fix']; if isinstance(fix_val, str) and fix_val: entry['fix'] = fix_val; else: logger.warning(...)`. This checks key presence (not truthiness) so absent fix is unchanged, and validates type+emptiness for present fix.
recommended_approach.logging: Add `import logging` and `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` to shared/egg_config/validators.py. Use logger.warning with a descriptive message including the check name and the invalid value, matching the style used in repo_config.py.
recommended_approach.fallback_alignment: Apply the identical fix_validation_logic to both ImportError fallback copies in config/repo_config.py (uses existing logger) and orchestrator/routes/pipelines/__init__.py (uses existing logger).
recommended_approach.test_updates: Update test_values_coerced_to_strings to expect fix: 3 to be dropped (not coerced). Extend test_empty_fix_dropped to verify warnings. Add tests for: valid string accepted, false/0 rejected with warning, list rejected with warning, absent key unchanged.

implementation_plan.scope_boundary: Tightly scoped to the fix key handling. No changes to name/command coercion, full_command handling, or surrounding validators.

open_questions.resolution: not_operator_grade — full_command has the same pattern but issue #3630 explicitly scopes to fix key only. full_command left unchanged.
not_operator_grade — name and command str()-coercion left unchanged per 'Do not refactor the surrounding validators'.
not_operator_grade — invalid fix values drop just the fix key, not the entire check entry. The entry still has valid name and command, so it remains usable.

risk_assessment.risk: Existing configs with non-string fix values (e.g. YAML lists) that previously produced broken shell commands now get a warning and the fix is dropped — strict improvement since the coercion was already broken.
risk_assessment.mitigation: The warning surfaces at load time; operators can fix their config.

risk_assessment.risk: False positive on falsy-but-valid fix values
risk_assessment.mitigation: String '0' is non-empty and truthy, so it is correctly retained. Only actual non-strings or empty strings are rejected.

risk_assessment.risk: Test test_values_coerced_to_strings breaks because fix: 3 is no longer coerced to '3'
risk_assessment.mitigation: Test is updated to expect fix: 3 to be dropped, matching the new behavior.

risk_assessment.risk: Fallback copies in repo_config.py and orchestrator drift from the primary
risk_assessment.mitigation: All three copies are updated identically; the fallbacks are ImportError-only edge cases.

binding_invariants: Only the fix key handling changes — name, command, and full_command coercion are unchanged.
When fix is present and is a non-empty string, it is retained as-is (no str() coercion needed since it's already a string).
When fix is present but not a non-empty string, a warning is logged and the fix key is dropped from the entry (the entry itself is retained).
When fix key is absent, the entry has no fix key (unchanged behavior).
All three copies of validate_checks are aligned.
